clue.text: The man with newspaper in lift

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A man with a newspaper rides up in an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Heft as a verb means to lift something up, especially to judge its weight.

clue.text: Dreadful choir types who only render lip service?

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters are in a terrible mess

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad choristers merely mouth the words rather than sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocrites profess beliefs they do not hold, paying mere lip service.

clue.text: Thief's accomplice receives excellent porcelain

indicators.note: the accomplice takes the excellent letters inside

parts.note: a fence receives and sells stolen goods
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fence takes in some fine stolen china.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is glazed earthenware or porcelain decorated with coloured glazes.

clue.text: Flattery to get round unemotional, inwardly hard teacher

indicators.note: the flattery word surrounds the other pieces, as if getting round them

parts.note: smarm is oily, ingratiating flattery

indicators.note: the hard letter goes inside the word for unemotional

parts.note: cool means calm and unemotional
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A stern teacher is won over by flattery despite being cool and hard inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmarm is an old-fashioned, often prim female schoolteacher.

clue.text: Betrayed in trick, getting furious inside

indicators.note: the furious word goes within the trick word

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
heated means angry, furious

explanation.surface: Someone tricked by a partner is furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated on is to have one's partner be unfaithful, a form of betrayal.

clue.text: Manager's heading off to a Glyndebourne production

indicators.note: the manager word loses its first letter

parts.note: a coper is one who copes, that is, manages; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: The manager heads off to see a show at Glyndebourne.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is an English country house in Sussex famous for its summer opera festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyndebourne stages musical dramas each summer, so its productions are of this genre.

clue.text: Game plan is not working out for Midlands town

indicators.note: working something out reshuffles the pieces into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A failing game plan for a Midlands football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Leamington Spa is a spa town in Warwickshire in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Usual disaster admitting man, heartless old boy

indicators.note: the rearranged word lets the other letters in
a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters are jumbled
the middle of man is removed, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: A usual calamity befalls a cruel former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former pupil, called an old boy at British schools.

clue.text: What sounds like nasty aspect

indicators.note: signals a word pronounced the same as another

parts.note: mean means nasty, unkind

explanation.surface: A question about something with an unpleasant look.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or appearance, their aspect.

clue.text: Run into difficulty that may be a bit of a pain

indicators.note: the run letter is put into the word for difficulty

parts.note: to be in a pickle is to be in difficulty
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Getting into trouble can be somewhat painful.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle is a slight stinging sensation, a mild pain.

clue.text: Claimant spoke, stirring tea-leaves compulsively

indicators.note: stirring mixes things, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claimant spoke while stirring tea leaves in the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea-leaf is rhyming slang for thief, so 'tea-leaves compulsively' means compulsive thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomaniacs have an irresistible urge to steal, being compulsive thieves.

clue.text: Effect of surface damage certain to occur after a time

indicators.note: the word for certain is placed following the word for a time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Damage to a surface will certainly show up after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a mark left where something has been rubbed out from a surface.

clue.text: Application gets prisoner money allowance

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a cent is a small coin, a piece of money
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A convict is granted a monetary allowance after applying.
explanation.definitionFit: Application in the sense of diligent focused effort means close mental attention.

clue.text: Pollution reduction? Put my record in

indicators.note: the record phrase is placed inside the reduction word

parts.note: a dent in profits is a reduction
to put my name on record is to file me

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have their reduction of pollution entered in the records.
explanation.definitionFit: Defilement is the act of making something dirty or impure.

clue.text: Like some gases put in to flush out last of badgers

indicators.note: flushing out removes a letter from the phrase for put in

parts.note: to put in is to insert

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of badgers

explanation.surface: Gases are pumped into a sett to drive the badgers out.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert gases, also called noble gases, are chemically unreactive.

clue.text: State control of economy? Trick is to get in money

indicators.note: the trick and is are placed inside the coin

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin
to rig is to manipulate by trickery
taken as written

explanation.surface: The trick to state control of the economy is getting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigisme is an economic policy of strong central state direction, the French term for state intervention.

clue.text: Engineers attending vehicle that springs back in reverse?

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Army engineers stand by a vehicle that bounces backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is something that draws or springs back, retracting.

clue.text: English meat isn't cooked in French restaurant

indicators.note: cooking alters ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In a French restaurant, English meat is not on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar serving food and drink.

clue.text: Agricultural work unfavourable in various times

indicators.note: the unfavourable word sits within the time pieces

parts.note: T is short for time, and an age is a long time
an age is a long period of time
ill means unfavourable, as in an ill omen

explanation.surface: Farm labour proves unrewarding through the seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the preparation of land by ploughing for growing crops.

clue.text: Daggers concealed by vile boys going around

indicators.note: the letters run backwards, as if turning round
the letters lie within the words vile boys

explanation.surface: Wicked lads are hiding knives as they roam about.
explanation.walkthrough: The run read backwards in VILE BOYS is SYOBELIV, which contains the five letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger symbols used in printing to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Specimen test —- appeal if not getting top grade

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the top grade letter, as in an A mark, is taken away from the appeal word

parts.note: a plea is an earnest appeal

explanation.surface: A sample test paper offers an appeal if a student misses the top mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a specimen typical of its group.

clue.text: Individual celebrity, say, in Texas

parts.note: lone means single, individual
a star is a celebrity
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A single famous person found in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is the nickname of Texas, after the single star on its flag.

clue.text: Superficial brightness of drunk's noticed

indicators.note: a drunk slurs an s into sh

parts.note: seen means noticed

explanation.surface: A drunk has spotted a shiny surface.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs 'seen' as if with SH in place of S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft lustre or shine on a surface.

clue.text: Wife -— troublemaker or doormat?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

explanation.surface: Is a wife a troublemaker or a pushover?
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a feeble, submissive person, as is a wimp.

clue.text: Confession of friend in Muslim leader's office

parts.note: a confession of being something begins I'm a
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend makes a confession in the office of a Muslim leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a statement: 'I'm a mate' is the confession of a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the office or rule of an imam, a Muslim leader.

clue.text: Tread right back, having taken enough

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is read backwards

parts.note: ample means more than enough

explanation.surface: Retracing one's steps after having had enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something, crushing it underfoot.

clue.text: Subsistence workers to receive pound — is that a joke?

indicators.note: the workers take the pound inside

parts.note: the peasantry are small farmers living at subsistence level
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Peasant farmers getting a pound would think it a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joking remark.

clue.text: Fingered material

definitions.meaning: fingered means touched or handled, past tense of feel

explanation.definitionFit: Felt is both the past tense of feel, to touch with fingers, and a matted cloth.
